text:
Roman Kantserov came over from the KHL after a 36-goal season with Metallurg Magnitogorsk, and the 22-year-old has not needed long. He has nine goals in his first 20 NHL games, six in his last ten, and a point streak that CBS Sports had at eight games on Nov. 8 and that ran through Nov. 12. The Athletic's Scott Powers noted him on the Blackhawks' top line beside Connor Bedard on Nov. 16, playing close to 19 minutes a night.

The finishing is the part to treat with care. Nine goals on 4.72 expected (the quality of his chances) is a 28% shooting rate, nearly double the top of his talent range. His chances are real, and that rate rarely survives a season.

The bigger concern is the other end. Chicago gets only 37.72% of expected goals at 5v5 with him on, and the team is worse with him than without. He has one assist and no goals in his last two games. For a second-round pick, 0.60 points a game beats the median of 0.30 for forwards drafted where he was. What to watch: whether the chances keep coming once the goals slow down.
headline: Roman Kantserov, rookie goal scorer on Connor Bedard's line
